text:
Dylan Guenther came into this season as a 40-goal scorer, and the numbers say that player is still in there. Through 19 games he has 6 goals and 12 points for the Mammoth, nine of them on the power play, and his chances (6.38 expected goals, about 1.17 per 60 minutes) sit almost exactly where they were last year. He is finishing a little below his usual rate, nothing alarming.

The worry is the stretch since early November. He has 3 points in his last ten games against roughly 7 our numbers expected, and he just came off injured reserve. That is a slump built partly on bad luck: Utah has scored about four fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains why we'd keep faith: last season he got 7.2 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net, 92nd percentile. Players who live there tend to get paid back. Our range for his season still runs 24 to 40 goals.
